data_output.description: data.py remains unchanged and returns encoded[split] as (features, labels, user_ids, row_ids), with features shaped (n, 5), labels from the existing long_view field, user_ids aligned row-for-row, and row_ids preserving canonical source order for train, valid, and test.

model_input.description: model.py receives Model.step(features, labels, user_ids), where features are the existing five-column encoded inputs, labels are the same displayed-impression long_view targets used for RankNet and BCE, and user_ids define within-user pairs. Model.predict receives features only and returns one finite score per input row.

model_designer.objective: Implement the requested hybrid training loss in model.py by adding a fixed-weight pointwise BCE anchor to the existing within-user RankNet objective over the same displayed impressions.
required_changes: In Model.step, retain the existing within-user positive-versus-negative RankNet pair construction and gradients exactly, and additionally compute pointwise binary cross-entropy for every row in the supplied features/labels batch using logits and labels, with numerically stable BCE and fixed coefficient 0.10.

Add the BCE gradient to each row gradient before feature-weight and bias updates: BCE row derivative is sigmoid(logit) - label, normalized over all displayed rows; preserve the existing RankNet normalization over pair_count, so the combined row gradient is the RankNet contribution plus 0.10 times the pointwise BCE contribution.
Do not return early when pair_count is zero: update from the BCE term alone in that case, while reporting the weighted combined loss.

Report total_loss as the existing mean RankNet loss plus 0.10 times mean BCE over all supplied rows; preserve the existing optimizer, learning-rate handling, L2 regularization, state format, logits, predict, and checkpoint compatibility.
Do not modify data.py, train.py, or config.json; the BCE weight must be implemented as the loss-term coefficient in model.py rather than as a configuration default.
preserve: Use the existing additive ID architecture and all five encoded input fields unchanged.
Keep within-user grouping, positive/negative definitions, pairwise RankNet sigmoid gradients, Adam moments, L2 regularization, and batch sampling behavior unchanged.
Keep validation-only within_user_auc checkpoint selection and early stopping unchanged; no test labels or test-derived values may enter training or selection.
Keep prediction behavior unchanged so the fixed training command emits predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz with exactly row_ids and scores in canonical validation and test row order.
coordination_notes: Model.step continues to receive features, labels, and user_ids from train.py; labels are the existing long_view values loaded by data.py, and the BCE term must use those same displayed impressions as the RankNet term.
The model input contract is features shaped (n, 5), labels shaped (n,), and user_ids shaped (n,); do not add feature columns or reinterpret any raw source field.
Do not use ground-truth test labels. The fixed evaluator alone loads ground truth.
The exact ablation is loss-only: retain features, architecture, optimizer, group sampling, split, and validation early stopping, adding only fixed BCE weight 0.10.

reasoning: Only model_designer is activated because the requested ablation changes exclusively the owned loss implementation in model.py. No feature, data contract, training-loop, or configuration change is required.
